title: Countably normed algebra and continuity of multiplication
notes: The notes write \(\|xy\|_i\leq\|x\|_k\|y\|_\ell\) for a countably normed ring \(R\).
statement: A countably normed complex algebra is an algebra with a Hausdorff locally convex topology defined by a countable family of norms. The displayed condition, interpreted as: for each \(i\) there exist \(k,\ell\) such that it holds for all \(x,y\), implies joint continuity of multiplication. Completeness makes this a Fr\'echet algebra. For the subsequent moment question one additionally needs a commutative algebra, a continuous involution and a specified continuous dual.
reconstruction: The quantifiers and the distinction between complete and incomplete algebras are supplied. No assumption that every norm is submultiplicative is inserted.
fate: The definition is the setting of the question, not a new theorem. Modern comparisons distinguish the topology from the positivity cone; see \citet[\S\S2.2--2.3]{infusino2024moment}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains standard terminology, with completeness and involution hypotheses to be stated separately.

title: Positive functionals as integrals over Hermitian characters
notes: A theorem labelled Gelfand--Naimark says \(f(x^*x)\geq0\Rightarrow f(x)=\int x(M)\,d\sigma(M)\), with \(M\) symmetric maximal ideals.
statement: For a unital commutative complex \(C^*\)-algebra \(A\), every positive linear functional \(L\) is uniquely \(L(a)=\int_{X(A)}\chi(a)\,d\mu(\chi)\), where \(X(A)\) is the compact space of unital characters and \(\mu\) is a finite positive regular Borel measure. Every character is Hermitian: \(\chi(a^*)=\overline{\chi(a)}\).
reconstruction: The precise \(C^*\)-algebra version is used to avoid attributing the assertion to arbitrary normed noncommutative rings. The notebook's symmetric maximal ideals correspond to kernels of Hermitian characters in the commutative setting.
fate: This is the classical representation paradigm explicitly invoked by the notes. Its infinite-dimensional moment analogues require additional positivity or continuity assumptions; \citet[Abstract]{schmudgen2018moment}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated classical version is established; the literal phrase ``normed ring does not specify adequate hypotheses.

title: Axioms ensuring moment representations in countably normed algebras
notes: \ru{Перенос --- ? (Не всегда: надо охар. аксиомат. класс).} The question asks when the preceding representation extends.
statement: Fix the convention that \(A\) is a commutative unital complex Fr\'echet \(*\)-algebra: its topology is Hausdorff, complete and defined by countably many norms, multiplication is jointly continuous, and the involution is continuous. Let \(X_h(A)\) be its continuous unital Hermitian characters with the weak topology. Characterize those \(A\) for which every continuous complex-linear functional \(L\) satisfying \(L(a^*a)\ge0\) for every \(a\in A\) has a finite positive Radon measure \(\mu_L\) on \(X_h(A)\) such that \(L(a)=\int\chi(a)\,d\mu_L(\chi)\) for all \(a\in A\). All character evaluations in this identity must be integrable. This is a universal property of the algebra, not a question about one chosen \(L\).
reconstruction: Commutativity, the unit, completeness, continuity of the involution and restriction to continuous characters fix one explicit version of the notebook's proposed axiomatization. These choices are supplied by the editor; the notes do not uniquely determine all of them. Cylinder-measure representation is weaker than the stated Radon representation.
fate: \citet[Abstract]{schmudgen2018moment}, circulated in December 2017, treats cylinder-measure representations under stronger positivity or Carleman assumptions. \citet[\S\S2.2--2.3]{infusino2024moment}, circulated in January 2023 and published in 2024, gives Radon criteria for algebras generated by a nuclear space. These results address specified hypotheses, not every algebra in the notebook.
present_status: As of November 2026, the opened literature supplies sufficient representation criteria in specified nuclear and moment-determinate settings, but those results do not give a characterization of the exact universal property stated here. The incomplete part is the passage from hypotheses on one functional or on a specified nuclear presentation to an algebra-level criterion quantifying over every continuous squares-positive functional. This audit does not establish that the reconstructed characterization is a generally accepted open conjecture, and the uncertainty about the notebook's intended category is retained explicitly.
worth: A bounded comparison within a specified nuclear Fr\'echet class is worth developing because it can determine which functional-level hypotheses follow from the algebra; a full general characterization is not proposed as a tractable new research claim.

title: Convolution algebra and Bochner representation
notes: The example is \(L^1\) with convolution and \(x^*(t)=\overline{x(-t)}\), followed by the Fourier integral of a positive measure.
statement: For the additive group \(\mathbb R\), a bounded continuous positive-definite function \(\varphi\) is the Fourier transform \(\varphi(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{it\lambda}\,d\mu(\lambda)\) of a unique finite positive measure. It defines a bounded positive functional on \(L^1(\mathbb R)\) by \(L(f)=\int f(t)\varphi(t)\,dt\), up to the chosen Fourier-sign convention.
reconstruction: The notebook does not distinguish the function being transformed from the argument of the functional; the two roles are separated here.
fate: The notes identify this as Bochner's already known theorem. It supplies a concrete spectral model for the preceding moment question, rather than an additional generalization.
present_status: As of November 2026, the example is standard and does not settle the countably normed case.

title: Fibre product by its universal property
notes: An object \(V=V_1\times_U V_2\) is drawn with commuting projections and a unique factorization from every test object.
statement: Given \(V_1\to U\leftarrow V_2\), the fibre product represents the functor \(W\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(W,V_1)\times_{\operatorname{Hom}(W,U)}\operatorname{Hom}(W,V_2)\). It is unique up to unique isomorphism, when it exists, and depends on the two morphisms to \(U\), not only on the three objects.
fate: Expository category theory; compare \citet[p.~38, footnote]{mumford1965picard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is the standard definition.

title: Grothendieck pretopology
notes: The notebook specifies a category, distinguished covering families, fibre products, identity covers, composition and base change.
statement: A pretopology is a class of families \(\{U_i\to U\}\) containing isomorphisms as covers, stable under composition of covering families and under pullback along every morphism, whenever the required pullbacks exist. It generates a Grothendieck topology of covering sieves.
reconstruction: ``Pretopology distinguishes these covering-family axioms from the equivalent sieve-based formulation; it does not change the notes' content.
fate: Already standard; \citet[p.~38]{mumford1965picard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the definition remains in use.

title: Local-homeomorphism site of a space
notes: For an ordinary topological space, objects are spaces locally homeomorphic to it; coverings are surjective families.
statement: For a space \(X\), take local homeomorphisms \(U\to X\), maps over \(X\), and jointly surjective families as covers. Fibre products over \(X\) exist and remain local homeomorphisms. Ordinary open subsets form a basis of this site, yielding the same category of sheaves as the usual topology of \(X\).
reconstruction: The structural map to the fixed base \(X\) and joint surjectivity are made explicit.
fate: Expository enlargement of ordinary topology; \citet[\S1 and pp.~44--45]{mumford1965picard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the comparison is standard.

title: Fibre products of circular coverings
notes: The circular example says \(U\times_U U=U\) and compares coverings of degrees two and three.
statement: If both maps \(S^1\to S^1\) have degree two, their pullback is the disjoint union of two circles, each mapping by degree two to either factor. For degrees \(m,n>0\), it has \(\gcd(m,n)\) components and each component covers the common base with degree \(\operatorname{lcm}(m,n)\). In particular degrees two and three give one degree-six covering.
reconstruction: The equation \(U\times_U U\cong U\) is valid for identity structure maps; it is false for two copies of the degree-two cover suggested by the drawing. The unclear arrow labels are not silently repaired.
fate: The corrected calculation follows directly from the pullback definition: pairs satisfy \(z^m=w^n\). It is an elementary emendation, not later research.
present_status: As of November 2026, the mathematical alternatives are settled, but the exact unlabelled arrows in the drawing remain ambiguous.

title: Presheaves and the sheaf equalizer condition
notes: A presheaf assigns abelian groups contravariantly; compatible local sections must glue uniquely for a sheaf.
statement: An abelian presheaf on a site \(\mathcal C\) is a functor \(F:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Ab}\). It is a sheaf when, for every cover, \(F(U)\to\prod_iF(U_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}F(U_i\times_UU_j)\) is an equalizer. This combines uniqueness and existence of descent.
fate: Expository; \citet[p.~39]{mumford1965picard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is the standard sheaf axiom.

title: Augmented Cech complex
notes: The groups are indexed \(C^0=P(U), C^1=\prod P(U_i), C^2=\prod P(U_i\times_UU_j)\), with alternating restrictions.
statement: The augmented complex is \(F(U)\to\check C^0(\mathcal U,F)\to\check C^1(\mathcal U,F)\to\cdots\), where \(\check C^r=\prod_{i_0,\ldots,i_r}F(U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{i_r})\) and the differential is the alternating sum of omitted-factor pullbacks. A sheaf makes the first two terms exact; higher exactness needs an acyclic cover or another additional hypothesis.
reconstruction: The notebook shifts the augmented complex by one compared with common modern \v{C}ech notation. No assertion that every cover computes derived cohomology is added.
fate: The construction belongs to the pre-existing sheaf formalism; \citet[\S1]{mumford1965picard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the indexing convention is harmless when stated.

title: Derived-functor cohomology of a site
notes: Global sections are left exact and their derived functors define cohomology.
statement: For a site with terminal object \(e\), \(\Gamma(F)=F(e)\) on abelian sheaves is left exact. The category has enough injectives, and \(H^q(\mathcal C,F)=R^q\Gamma(F)\). Without a representable terminal object one uses the terminal sheaf to define global sections.
reconstruction: The existence of enough injectives and the terminal-object convention are supplied.
fate: Expository; \citet[pp.~37,39]{mumford1965picard}; see also \citet[\S\S2--3]{grothendieck1957homological}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the definition is established.

title: An announced finite-group example
notes: The last line announces a topology associated with representations of a finite group, without giving its objects or covers.
statement: No precise theorem is recoverable from this line alone. A natural later comparison is the site of \(\Gamma\)-sets with jointly surjective covers, whose abelian sheaves are \(\Gamma\)-modules; this is explicitly constructed in record 151.
reconstruction: The \(\Gamma\)-set interpretation is a cross-reference, not a replacement for the missing February construction.
fate: Compare \citet[pp.~39--41]{mumford1965picard} and occurrences 1968-151.2--1968-151.4; the isolated phrase does not establish that this was the exact category intended.
present_status: As of November 2026, the later example is identified, while this announcement remains incomplete.

title: Enveloping algebra, centre and differential-operator realization
notes: \(U(\mathfrak g)\) is generated by \(e_i\) with \([e_i,e_j]=\sum c_{ij}^ke_k\); central elements are called Laplace or Casimir operators. A group action yields differential operators, faithfully on the group itself.
statement: For a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\), \(U(\mathfrak g)=T(\mathfrak g)/(xy-yx-[x,y])\). If a Lie group with this Lie algebra acts smoothly or algebraically, differentiation gives a representation by differential operators, which may have a kernel. The representation by invariant differential operators on the group is faithful. For connected \(G\), the image of \(Z(U(\mathfrak g))\) commutes with the differentiated and group actions.
reconstruction: Connectedness is relevant to passage from infinitesimal to group invariance. PBW supplies the faithfulness assertion and the filtration underlying the later fractions.
fate: Background recalled in \citet[Introduction]{gelfandkirillov1966corps} and \citet[\S\S2--3]{gelfandkirillov1969structure}.
present_status: As of November 2026, these are standard algebraic constructions.

title: Faithfulness on the basic affine space
notes: The action of \(U(\mathfrak g)\) on \(N_-\backslash G\) is said to be faithful.
statement: Let \(G\) be a simply connected complex semisimple algebraic group and \(N_-\) a maximal unipotent subgroup. Right translation on \(\mathcal O(N_-\backslash G)\) differentiates to an injective homomorphism \(U(\mathfrak g)\to\mathcal D(N_-\backslash G)\). The coordinate ring contains every finite-dimensional irreducible representation, and these representations separate elements of \(U(\mathfrak g)\).
reconstruction: The algebraic category, regular functions and simply connected group are specified. ``Nilpotent group is replaced by the intended maximal unipotent subgroup.
fate: It is part of the representation-theoretic setup in \citet[\S\S3--6]{gelfandkirillov1969structure}, not the new fraction-field theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026, the statement is established.

title: Finite-translation functions and the compact-group completeness theorem
notes: A function is called regular when its translates span a finite-dimensional space; on a compact group such functions approximate all functions. The sine function on a line is an example.
statement: On a compact group, finite sums of matrix coefficients of continuous finite-dimensional representations are uniformly dense in continuous functions. For a complex semisimple algebraic group, regular functions are finite sums of algebraic matrix coefficients. The finite-translation characterization must be understood with the relevant continuity, holomorphicity or algebraicity conditions; on a real additive line, sine is representative but not a polynomial regular function.
reconstruction: The notebook uses ``regular across analytic and algebraic categories. These two meanings are distinguished.
fate: Classical representation-theoretic background; the algebraic formulation is recalled in \citet[\S3]{gelfandkirillov1969structure}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the density and algebraic matrix-coefficient statements are established in their specified categories.

title: Affinization and rationality of the basic affine space
notes: Take the invariant ring of functions \(f(n_-g)=f(g)\), its spectrum \(X\), and note that \(N_-\backslash G\) is birational to projective space.
statement: The basic affine space \(A=N_-\backslash G\) is quasi-affine; \(X=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O(G)^{N_-}\) is its affinization. The big Bruhat cell gives a dense open subset of \(A\) isomorphic to \(T\times N_+\), hence its function field is purely transcendental of degree \(\operatorname{rank}G+|\Phi^+|\). It is consequently rational, as is \(X\).
reconstruction: The quasi-affine quotient is not identified pointwise with its affine completion. ``Birational to projective space means rationality, not compactness.
fate: Explicit setup in \citet[\S\S3--4]{gelfandkirillov1969structure}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this construction and rationality are established.

title: Ore fractions of an enveloping algebra
notes: The notes stress the nontrivial existence of a division ring of quotients and that single fractions \(QP^{-1}\) suffice.
statement: PBW implies that \(U(\mathfrak g)\) is a left and right Noetherian domain. It satisfies both Ore conditions and embeds in its classical division ring \(D(\mathfrak g)\). Each element can be represented as a single right fraction \(QP^{-1}\), and also as a single left fraction, with nonzero denominator.
reconstruction: The Ore condition, rather than formal commutative fraction manipulation, justifies the two-step description.
fate: This repeats the theme of 1965-80.1--1965-80.3; see \citet[\S1]{gelfandkirillov1966corps}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction is standard for finite-dimensional Lie algebras in characteristic zero.

title: Weyl division rings with central parameters
notes: \(D_{n,k}\) uses \(x_i,\partial/\partial x_i\) and commuting parameters \(y_1,\ldots,y_k\); the two integers are invariants.
statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), define \(D_{n,k}=\operatorname{Frac}(A_n(\mathbb C)\otimes\mathbb C[y_1,\ldots,y_k])\), with \([\partial_i,x_j]=\delta_{ij}\) and all other generator commutators zero. Its centre is \(\mathbb C(y_1,\ldots,y_k)\). For a semisimple Lie algebra the proposed parameters are \(k=\operatorname{rank}\mathfrak g\), \(n=|\Phi^+|\), so \(2n+k=\dim\mathfrak g\).
reconstruction: The field and algebraic independence of central parameters are stated explicitly.
fate: Defined and its numerical invariants studied in \citet[\S\S1,4]{gelfandkirillov1966corps}; compare 1965-80.5--1965-80.6.
present_status: As of November 2026, the standard division rings and the distinction of their parameters are established.

title: The unextended Gelfand--Kirillov conjecture for semisimple algebras
notes: The conjectural isomorphism \(D(\mathfrak g)\simeq D_{n,k}\) is described as almost proved; a later parenthesis says that it is unknown for \(U\), except the unimodular case.
statement: For a complex semisimple Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\), ask whether \(\operatorname{Frac}U(\mathfrak g)\cong D_{|\Phi^+|,\operatorname{rank}\mathfrak g}\). This assertion concerns the original division ring, with no finite extension of its centre.
reconstruction: The historical term unimodular is read in its matrix-group sense \(SL_m\), not as the modern condition \(\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{ad}x)=0\), which every semisimple Lie algebra has.
fate: Type \(A\) was proved in \citet[\S3]{gelfandkirillov1966corps}. \citet[Theorem~1.1]{premet2010modular} disproved the conjecture for simple types \(B_\ell\;(\ell\ge3),D_\ell\;(\ell\ge4),E_6,E_7,E_8,F_4\). Premet states that the results were announced at the INI Algebraic Lie Theory final conference in June 2009; the preprint appeared on 15 July 2009 and the article in 2010.
present_status: As of November 2026, the blanket semisimple assertion is false. The cited 2013 discussion still lists types \(C\) and \(G_2\) as open; no later resolution of those cases was verified in this search. The commutative rationality theorem for \(G_2\) in \citet[Theorem~2]{anderson2013g2} is not a resolution of the division-ring conjecture.

title: Nilpotent and algebraic solvable cases
notes: For nilpotent algebras the conjecture is proved; for algebraic solvable algebras the speaker says ``probably.
statement: For a finite-dimensional nilpotent Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, its enveloping division ring is a Weyl division ring with central transcendental parameters, with \(k\) the index and \(2n=\dim\mathfrak g-k\). The notebook's assertion about all algebraic solvable algebras is a separate tentative extension.
reconstruction: The nilpotent theorem is isolated from the unproved-at-this-point solvable remark. No theorem for arbitrary nonalgebraic solvable Lie algebras is inferred.
fate: The nilpotent case is proved in \citet[\S2]{gelfandkirillov1966corps}. The precise publication intended by the tentative solvable parenthesis was not established in the sources opened for this item.
present_status: As of November 2026, the nilpotent assertion is established. This entry makes no comprehensive November 2026 classification claim for solvable Lie fields.

title: Central extension by virtual Laplace operators
notes: The new algebra is \(\widetilde U=U\otimes_Z\widetilde Z\); \(\widetilde Z/Z\) is called algebraic with Weyl Galois group.
statement: For a split semisimple Lie algebra in characteristic zero, the Harish-Chandra description identifies the centre with Weyl-invariant polynomials on a Cartan dual, using the shifted Weyl action. Adjoining the Cartan coordinate functions gives a finite central algebra extension \(\widetilde U\). On fraction fields the induced extension \(\mathbb C(\mathfrak h^*)/\mathbb C(\mathfrak h^*)^W\) is Galois with group \(W\). These added commuting coordinates are the virtual Laplace operators.
reconstruction: Galois is asserted for fraction fields; the extension of rings can ramify. The shift convention is part of the Harish-Chandra identification.
fate: This construction is developed in \citet[\S\S7--8]{gelfandkirillov1969structure}; the paper was received on 30 September 1968 and appeared in 1969.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction is established and remains distinct from the original enveloping algebra.

title: The Weyl fraction field after central extension
notes: The theorem explicitly states that the fraction division ring of \(\widetilde U(\mathfrak g)\) is \(D_{n,k}\).
statement: With \(\widetilde U\) the virtual-Laplace extension above, \(\operatorname{Frac}\widetilde U(\mathfrak g)\cong D_{n,k}\), where \(n=|\Phi^+|\) and \(k=\operatorname{rank}\mathfrak g\). The isomorphism is a statement after the prescribed finite extension of the centre.
reconstruction: The central extension is retained in both the hypothesis and conclusion.
fate: Exact publication match: \citet[\S13, Theorem~3]{gelfandkirillov1969structure}, received September 1968 and published in 1969.
present_status: As of November 2026, this theorem is established; its truth does not imply the unextended conjecture, which fails in several types.

title: Algebraic extensions of Weyl division rings
notes: \ru{Алг. расшир.} of \(D_{n,k}\) are queried, with algebraic varieties mentioned as the commutative analogy.
statement: The note asks for a geometric or structural understanding of extensions of \(D_{n,k}\), but specifies neither finite left/right degree, centrality, embeddings, nor the equivalence relation on extensions. These choices lead to different mathematical problems, so no unique classification assertion can be reconstructed.
reconstruction: The preceding central Galois extension is an example, not a definition of every extension meant by the question.
fate: \citet[Introduction and \S13]{gelfandkirillov1969structure} explains the motivating finite central extension. A precise general extension problem matching this one-line question was not identified.
present_status: As of November 2026, the remark remains under-specified; no purported solution of noncommutative birational geometry is assigned to it.

title: Global holomorphic differential operators on compact complex manifolds
notes: The question asks to describe regular differential operators on compact complex manifolds, followed by three vector fields on the Riemann sphere.
statement: For a compact complex manifold \(X\), study the filtered algebra \(H^0(X,\mathcal D_X)\), where \(\mathcal D_X\) consists of finite-order holomorphic differential operators acting on \(\mathcal O_X\). Its order-one part contains \(H^0(X,T_X)\) and constants; higher symbols lie in \(H^0(X,\operatorname{Sym}^m T_X)\), but not every symbol necessarily lifts.
reconstruction: This fixes ``regular as holomorphic and the coefficient bundle as trivial. The notebook gives no manifold class or requested invariant, so a universal classification target cannot be extracted.
fate: The differential-operator viewpoint is explained in \citet[Introduction]{gelfandkirillov1966corps}; its basic affine-space results do not answer this compact-manifold question.
present_status: As of November 2026, the object is meaningful, but the requested general classification is not precise enough to assign a solved/open theorem.

title: Global vector fields on the projective line
notes: The sphere has \(\partial_z,z\partial_z,z^2\partial_z\).
statement: Every global holomorphic vector field on \(\mathbb P^1\) has the form \((a+bz+cz^2)\partial_z\). In the coordinate \(w=1/z\), this becomes \(-(aw^2+bw+c)\partial_w\), which is regular at infinity. The three displayed fields form a basis of \(H^0(\mathbb P^1,T_{\mathbb P^1})\cong\mathfrak{sl}_2\).
reconstruction: The observation describes order-one operators; it does not itself classify all higher-order operators on all compact manifolds.
fate: This is the elementary sphere example in the notes. The coordinate calculation directly verifies its global regularity.
present_status: As of November 2026, the example is correct and established.

title: The first Weyl algebra
notes: The ring of quantum mechanics is generated by \(p,q\) with \([p,q]=1\).
statement: \(A_1(\mathbb C)=\mathbb C\langle p,q\rangle/(pq-qp-1)\), represented faithfully by \(p=d/dx\) and \(q=x\) on \(\mathbb C[x]\). Its monomials \(p^a q^b\), \(a,b\ge0\), form a vector-space basis. Its Ore fraction division ring is \(D_1\).
reconstruction: The commutator convention is fixed and maintained in the later eigenvalue calculation.
fate: The notation and algebra are those of \citet[\S1]{dixmier1968weyl}; compare 1965-80.5.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction is standard.

title: Polynomial shears generate the automorphism group of A1
notes: The automorphisms are generated by \(p\mapsto p, q\mapsto q+f(p)\) and \(q\mapsto q,p\mapsto p+g(q)\), or by one shear family and Fourier exchange.
statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), \(\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbb C}A_1\) is generated by the two polynomial shear families \((p,q)\mapsto(p,q+f(p))\), \((p,q)\mapsto(p+g(q),q)\). Equivalently, one may use \((p,q)\mapsto(p+g(q),q)\) together with \((p,q)\mapsto(-q,p)\); linear shears generate the required determinant-one linear transformations.
reconstruction: The statement is for automorphisms, not arbitrary endomorphisms. It does not assert the Dixmier endomorphism conjecture.
fate: This is explicitly an exposition of Dixmier's work, published in 1968: \citet[Theorem~8.10]{dixmier1968weyl}. The notebook supplies evidence that it circulated by 11 March 1968.
present_status: As of November 2026, the generation theorem is established.

title: Automorphisms of the Weyl division ring
notes: For \(D_{1,0}\), the analogous automorphism description is unknown.
statement: Describe \(\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbb C}D_1\), where \(D_1=\operatorname{Frac}A_1(\mathbb C)\). The subgroup stabilizing the rational function subfield \(\mathbb C(q)\) consists exactly of maps \(q\mapsto\theta(q)=(aq+b)/(cq+d)\), \(p\mapsto\theta^{\prime}(q)^{-1}p+r(q)\), where \(ad-bc\ne0\) and \(r\in\mathbb C(q)\). This subgroup does not exhaust the full problem.
reconstruction: The stabilizer formula is a precisely bounded modern result, not part of the notebook's assertion of ignorance.
fate: This repeats 1965-80.10 and retains GP-1965-08. \citet[\S5.3.3, final Remark, p.~66]{dumas2011invariants} gives the exact rational-subfield stabilizer and explicitly documents the unresolved full automorphism-group structure. The pseudodifferential-series embedding used in the elementary centralizer proof is described in \S5.2.2, pp.~59--60. These are known special results, not new research claims.
present_status: As of November 2026, no complete description of \(\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbb C}D_1\) was found in this audit; its open status is explicit in \citet[p.~66]{dumas2011invariants}. The checked 2026 result of \citet[Corollary~8.12]{lauritzenthomsen2026duality}, first posted on 11 October and revised on 2 November 2026, establishes equality of finite left and right indices for noncommutative division subrings. That theorem does not classify automorphisms and does not supersede the full-group question. The rational-subfield stabilizer remains a bounded, established reduction.
worth: Worth developing the rational-subfield stabilizer and its centralizer proof, because this gives a checkable reduction without claiming to classify all division-ring automorphisms.

title: Arnold: polynomial canonical maps and the Poisson bracket
notes: Arnold writes the usual two-variable Poisson bracket and considers polynomials \(P,Q\) for which it equals one.
statement: On \(\mathbb C^2\) with coordinates \(p,q\), \(\{P,Q\}=P_pQ_q-P_qQ_p\). If \(\{P,Q\}=1\), the polynomial map \((p,q)\mapsto(P,Q)\) has Jacobian determinant one and is locally biholomorphic and symplectic. If it is additionally a polynomial automorphism, it is a global polynomial canonical transformation.
reconstruction: The distinction between local invertibility and a global polynomial inverse is essential. The notes do not state or solve the Jacobian conjecture.
fate: The bracket calculation is the classical analogue offered in the seminar; \citet[Introduction and \S8]{dixmier1968weyl} provides the Weyl-algebra comparison.
present_status: As of November 2026, the local conclusion follows directly from the inverse-function theorem; no global-inverse claim is warranted.
speaker: V. I. Arnold

title: The qualified relationship with associated graded Poisson algebras
notes: The note says there is no connection, even with grading.
statement: For the Bernstein filtration \(\deg p=\deg q=1\), \(\operatorname{gr}A_1\cong\mathbb C[p,q]\), and the commutator induces its canonical Poisson bracket of degree \(-2\). A general polynomial shear need not preserve this filtration, so taking an associated graded map does not directly compare all automorphisms.
reconstruction: This distinguishes a valid warning about arbitrary automorphisms from the overly broad denial of any graded relationship.
fate: The filtered construction follows from the relation \([p,q]=1\); the Newton/degree analysis in \citet[\S\S2--3]{dixmier1968weyl} is relevant background.
present_status: As of November 2026, the blanket literal statement is false; the more restricted warning is correct.

title: Strictly semisimple elements and the missing affine parameters
notes: An element is completely semisimple when its adjoint has a complete eigenbasis; it is then said to be carried to \(pq\).
statement: For a nonscalar \(x\in A_1(\mathbb C)\) such that \(\operatorname{ad}x\) is diagonalizable on the whole algebra, there are an automorphism \(\alpha\), a nonzero \(a\in\mathbb C\), and \(b\in\mathbb C\) with \(\alpha(x)=a pq+b\). The coefficient and scalar term cannot generally be removed by an automorphism.
reconstruction: ``Complete system of eigenvalues is read as an eigenvector decomposition. Scalars are excluded from the strictly semisimple case.
fate: Exact corrected form: \citet[Theorem~9.2 and Corollary~9.3]{dixmier1968weyl}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the corrected theorem is established; the notebook's single normal form \(pq\) is too restrictive.

title: Eigenvalues of the Euler element under the stated commutator convention
notes: The formula gives \(p^a q^b\mapsto(a-b)p^a q^b\).
statement: With \([p,q]=1\), \([pq,p]=-p\), \([pq,q]=q\), hence \([pq,p^a q^b]=(b-a)p^a q^b\). Thus the Weyl monomials are eigenvectors of \(\operatorname{ad}(pq)\), with eigenvalues \(b-a\).
reconstruction: The sign is fixed by the preceding definition, not by a different convention silently substituted for it.
fate: Direct commutator computation confirms the correction; compare \citet[\S5.3, equation~(4)]{dixmier1968weyl}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the printed \(a-b\) has the opposite sign under the notebook's convention.

title: Commutative centralizers of nonscalar Weyl elements
notes: A result attributed to Amitsur says the centralizer \(C(x)\) is commutative.
statement: For every nonscalar \(x\in A_1(\mathbb C)\), \(C_{A_1}(x)\) is commutative. It is a finitely generated commutative algebra of transcendence degree one. For a scalar \(x\), its centralizer is all of \(A_1\), so that exception is necessary.
reconstruction: The nonscalar hypothesis and the precise ambient algebra are supplied; the note does not claim this for every arbitrary noncommutative algebra.
fate: \citet[\S4.2 and Theorem~5.1]{dixmier1968weyl} states the centralizer results and credits Amitsur for commutativity.
present_status: As of November 2026, the nonscalar theorem is established.

title: Elliptic and cuspidal centralizers
notes: The notes say centralizers need not be polynomial rings and display \(X^3=Y^2+\alpha\) for arbitrary \(\alpha\in\mathbb C\).
statement: There are commuting elements \(X,Y\in A_1(\mathbb C)\) satisfying \(Y^2=X^3-\alpha\), whose generated commutative algebra has that sole defining relation and occurs as a centralizer in Dixmier's construction. For \(\alpha\ne0\) this is the affine coordinate ring of a nonsingular elliptic curve with one point removed; for \(\alpha=0\) it is a cuspidal cubic ring, not \(\mathbb C[t]\).
reconstruction: Commutativity and absence of additional algebraic relations are needed for the geometric conclusion; the displayed equation by itself would not prove it.
fate: Exact family in \citet[\S\S5.5--5.6]{dixmier1968weyl}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the examples are established and refute the assertion that every nonscalar centralizer is a polynomial ring.

title: Weighted Dolbeault spaces and plurisubharmonic exhaustion
notes: The Levi form \(L(\phi)\) is nonnegative, and \(\|f\|_\phi^2=\int_\Omega |f|^2e^{-\phi}dV\). Compact sublevel sets are said to imply pseudoconvexity.
statement: For an open \(\Omega\subset\mathbb C^n\) and a real \(C^2\) function \(\phi\), its Levi form is \(\sum_{j,k}\phi_{j\bar k}\xi_j\overline{\xi_k}\). Nonnegativity is equivalent to plurisubharmonicity. The weighted space \(L^2_{p,q}(\Omega,e^{-\phi})\) consists of measurable forms with finite displayed norm. A plurisubharmonic exhaustion, whose sublevels are relatively compact, makes \(\Omega\) pseudoconvex.
reconstruction: Exhaustion is a global hypothesis; it does not follow from nonnegativity of the Levi form alone.
fate: These are the definitions used in \citet[\S\S2.1--2.2]{hormander1965l2}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the formulation is standard.

title: A weighted L2 solution with logarithmic loss
notes: For \(q\ge1\), \(\bar\partial f=0\) and \(f\in L^2(\phi)\), the notes claim \(\bar\partial g=f\), \(g\in L^2(\phi+2\log(1+|z|^2))\), and \(\sqrt q\|g\|\le\|f\|\).
statement: Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb C^n\) be pseudoconvex, \(\phi\in C^2(\Omega)\) plurisubharmonic, \(1\le q\le n\), and let \(f\) be a distributionally \(\bar\partial\)-closed \((p,q)\)-form with \(\int |f|^2e^{-\phi}<\infty\). Then a solution \(g\) satisfies \(\int |g|^2e^{-\phi}(1+|z|^2)^{-2}\le q^{-1}\int|f|^2e^{-\phi}\).
reconstruction: The norm on the left uses the modified weight, while that on the right uses the original weight. With the usual Euclidean coefficient norm, the lower Levi eigenvalue of \(2\log(1+|z|^2)\) even gives the stronger factor \(1/(2q)\); the displayed weaker inequality is therefore consistent.
fate: A direct specialization of \citet[Theorems~2.2.1 and 2.2.1\(^{\prime}\)]{hormander1965l2}, published three years before the seminar.
present_status: As of November 2026, the existence theorem is established with the specified weights.

title: Density of entire functions with weighted growth
notes: The union of entire functions in \(L^2(\phi+c\log(1+|z|^2))\) is called nontrivial and dense in all entire functions for compact convergence; the note identifies this with a pointwise exponential-polynomial bound.
statement: Fix \(\phi\) and define \(\mathcal A_\phi=\bigcup_{c>0}\{f\in\mathcal O(\mathbb C^n):\int|f|^2e^{-\phi}(1+|z|^2)^{-c}<\infty\}\). The recorded assertion is density of \(\mathcal A_\phi\) in \(\mathcal O(\mathbb C^n)\). Under the explicitly sufficient extra hypothesis that \(\phi\) is bounded below, every polynomial belongs to this union, so density follows from Taylor approximation. For arbitrary weights, integral and pointwise bounds require their precise regularization and factor-of-two conventions.
reconstruction: The bounded-below case is a verified elementary reconstruction, not asserted as the entire intended theorem. The quoted pointwise bound \(e^\phi\) cannot simply be substituted for the weight \(e^{-\phi}\) in an \(L^2\) norm.
fate: \citet[Theorem~2.3.5 and Corollary~2.3.6]{hormander1965l2} gives a precise Runge approximation theorem, but its statement is not the identical fixed-growth-class assertion. The exact version intended here was not established from the opened source.
present_status: As of November 2026, the elementary bounded-below case is settled; the full intended growth-weight statement remains unidentified in this audit.

title: Martineau: realization of regularized growth indicators
notes: The notebook attributes to ``Martino'' the assertion that indicators are all radially homogeneous plurisubharmonic functions, with \(i(z)=\lim_{\tau\to\infty}\tau^{-k}\log|f(\tau z)|\).
statement: Fix \(\rho>0\). For an entire function \(f\) on \(\mathbb C^n\) satisfying \(|f(z)|\le C\exp(A|z|^\rho)\), form the radial upper indicator \(h_f(z)=\limsup_{r\to\infty}r^{-\rho}\log|f(rz)|\) and its upper-semicontinuous regularization \(h_f^*\). The regularized indicators, allowing the identically minus-infinity case for the zero function, are exactly the plurisubharmonic functions positively homogeneous of degree \(\rho\): \(h(tz)=t^\rho h(z)\) for \(t>0\). Thus any such nontrivial \(h\) is realized by an entire function of the indicated finite growth order.
reconstruction: The limsup, upper-semicontinuous regularization and finite-type growth convention are essential. The scan's stroke above lim is too unclear to certify a transcription correction. The precise theorem uses one plurisubharmonic condition; the English phrase ``plurisubharmonic harmonic'' must not be read as imposing harmonicity as well.
fate: Exact identification: \citet[Theorem~1, p.~8-02]{martineau1966croissance}. The title page dates the lecture 6 June 1966 and the redaction June 1967, both before the seminar. The introduction acknowledges errors in the earlier presentation and subsequent corrections; the opened corrected exposition is the source used here. This is not the different P\'olya--Ehrenpreis--Martineau theorem on analytic functionals.
present_status: As of November 2026, the regularized-indicator characterization is established. The unregularized ordinary-limit reading is not the theorem.

title: Convexity of weights depending only on real parts
notes: If \(\phi=\phi(x)\), it is plurisubharmonic exactly when it is convex; the notes also recall subharmonicity on complex lines.
statement: Let \(\phi(z)=u(\operatorname{Re}z)\), with \(u\in C^2(\mathbb R^n,\mathbb R)\). Then \(\phi_{z_j\bar z_k}=\frac14u_{x_jx_k}\); thus \(\phi\) is plurisubharmonic exactly when \(u\) is convex. More generally a continuous function is plurisubharmonic exactly when its restriction to every complex affine line is subharmonic wherever defined.
reconstruction: The regularity is stated for the Hessian proof; the distributional formulation extends the equivalence.
fate: This is standard background for the weights in \citet[\S2.2]{hormander1965l2}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the statement is established.

title: Solving d-bar with exponential type and polynomial growth
notes: For \(\bar\partial u=f\) on the plane, \(|f(z)|\le C e^{a|\operatorname{Im}z|}(1+|z|^2)^k\); a solution in this growth class is called nontrivial.
statement: For measurable \(f\) satisfying this bound, with \(a\ge0\) and finite \(k\), the weighted \(L^2\) method gives a distributional solution with the same exponential type and a possibly larger polynomial exponent. One chooses a plurisubharmonic weight comparable to \(2a|\operatorname{Im}z|+c\log(1+|z|^2)\); the logarithmic loss is absorbed by increasing \(c\).
reconstruction: The phrase ``this class'' is interpreted as allowing some polynomial exponent, not preserving the exact given \(k\). Interior estimates or a local Cauchy decomposition are needed to convert the weighted integral estimate to pointwise growth.
fate: This illustrates \citet[\S2.4]{hormander1965l2}, rather than a new independent theorem of Palamodov.
present_status: As of November 2026, the growth-class solvability is established with a polynomial loss; no fixed-exponent estimate is claimed.

title: The bounded right-hand-side assertion on the unit disc
notes: The notes say that for bounded \(f\) on the unit disc, \(\partial_z u=f\) (or \(\partial_{\bar z}u=f\)) need not have a bounded solution.
statement: For every \(f\in L^\infty(\mathbb D)\), \(u(z)=\pi^{-1}\int_{\mathbb D}f(\zeta)/(z-\zeta)\,dA(\zeta)\) solves \(\bar\partial u=f\) distributionally and satisfies \(\|u\|_\infty\le4\|f\|_\infty\). Conjugating the kernel gives the corresponding result for \(\partial_z\). Thus the recorded nonexistence claim is false without another omitted requirement, such as a boundary condition or a different data norm.
reconstruction: The scan confirms the negative assertion. The denominator's bar ambiguity does not rescue it, since both operators have the same bounded-data conclusion.
fate: The correction follows from \(\bar\partial(1/(\pi z))=\delta_0\) and the bound \(\mathbb D\subset B(z,2)\), \(\pi^{-1}\int_{B(z,2)}|z-\zeta|^{-1}dA=4\). This is an elementary verification, not a later solution of a research problem.
present_status: As of November 2026, the literal assertion is refuted by the displayed solution operator.

title: A measure-growth condition of Carleson type
notes: A measure \(f\) is drawn near the disc boundary with \(|f(S\cap\Omega)|\le C R_S\), said to suffice for solvability.
statement: A standard precise growth condition would be \(|\mu|(B(\zeta,r)\cap\mathbb D)\le Cr\) for boundary-centred discs, where \(|\mu|\) is total variation. The notebook does not specify disc centres, total variation, boundary versus interior boundedness, or the solution's trace. Those choices are essential to a \(\bar\partial\) theorem with measure data.
reconstruction: The name ``Carleson type'' describes the scaling; it is not an exact identification with a corona theorem or a bounded-interior solution theorem.
fate: Searches for the displayed measure condition and bounded \(\bar\partial\) solvability did not determine a unique theorem matching the drawing. The nearby \(L^2\) theorem in \citet[\S2.2]{hormander1965l2} does not by itself establish this measure-data statement.
present_status: As of November 2026, the intended norm and measure theorem remain unidentified.

title: The boundary signature condition aq
notes: On the complex tangent hyperplane, the Levi form has at least \(q+1\) negative or \(n-q\) positive eigenvalues.
statement: For a defining function \(\rho\) with \(d\rho\ne0\) on \(\partial\Omega\), condition \(a_q\) requires that the Hermitian form \(\partial\bar\partial\rho\) restricted to \(\ker\partial\rho\) have at least \(q+1\) strictly negative eigenvalues or at least \(n-q\) strictly positive eigenvalues at each boundary point, with \(\Omega=\{\rho<0\}\).
reconstruction: The normal orientation and strictness are fixed. The complex tangent space has dimension \(n-1\).
fate: Exact definition in \citet[Definition~3.3.4]{hormander1965l2}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the condition is established terminology for the ensuing estimates.

title: Pseudoconvexity and the incorrect index a0
notes: The boundary is called pseudoconvex if \(a_0\) holds, glossed as \(n-1\) positive eigenvalues.
statement: A \(C^2\) boundary is Levi pseudoconvex if the tangential Levi form is nonnegative. Strict pseudoconvexity means all \(n-1\) tangential eigenvalues are positive; this is the positive branch of \(a_1\), and it implies \(a_q\) for \(q\ge1\). It is not the positive branch of \(a_0\), which would demand \(n\) positive eigenvalues on an \((n-1)\)-dimensional space.
reconstruction: Both the index and the distinction between weak and strict pseudoconvexity must be corrected.
fate: Compare \citet[Definition~3.3.4 and Theorem~3.5.1]{hormander1965l2}; the notebook's index is inconsistent with its immediately preceding definition.
present_status: As of November 2026, the literal identification is false; the corrected strict-pseudoconvex statement is standard.

title: Finite-dimensional weighted cohomology and closed range
notes: For a bounded domain with \(C^3\) boundary satisfying \(a_q\), the cohomology is finite dimensional and the image is closed.
statement: Let \(\Omega\) be relatively compact in a Hermitian complex \(n\)-manifold, with \(C^3\) boundary satisfying \(a_q\), and let the real weight be continuous on \(\overline\Omega\). For the maximal weak \(\bar\partial\) operators in the \((p,q-1),(p,q),(p,q+1)\) weighted \(L^2\) spaces, \(\operatorname{im}\bar\partial\) at degree \(q\) is closed, and \(\ker\bar\partial/\operatorname{im}\bar\partial\) at degree \(q\) is finite dimensional.
reconstruction: The Hilbert-space domains and the weight's boundary control are supplied; arbitrary singular weights are not covered by this statement.
fate: Exact match with \citet[Theorem~3.4.1]{hormander1965l2}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the theorem is established under these boundary and weight hypotheses.

title: Gelfand asks about domains of regularity
notes: \ru{Гельфанд: области регулярности --- ?} Palamodov reportedly says that nobody is working on this.
statement: The phrase does not identify a function space, operator domain, boundary regularity scale or necessary-and-sufficient condition. It could concern solvability domains or regularity of solutions, but no unique mathematical question can be recovered.
reconstruction: No identification with later global regularity of the \(\bar\partial\)-Neumann problem, or with a particular counterexample, is made.
fate: The surrounding lecture has the definite scope of \citet[\S3.4]{hormander1965l2}; its literature does not determine which additional question Gelfand meant. The historical report about other researchers is not accepted as a verified priority claim.
present_status: As of November 2026, the intended question remains unrecoverable from this sentence.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Global exhaustion and vanishing in a fixed degree
notes: A real function \(\Psi\) on the whole domain, with one more positive Levi direction, is said to force zero cohomology.
statement: Let \(X\) be a complex \(n\)-manifold with a \(C^2\) exhaustion \(\Psi\). Assume that outside a compact sublevel its regular levels satisfy \(a_q\), and everywhere its full Levi form has at least \(q+1\) negative or at least \(n-q+1\) positive eigenvalues. Then \(H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)=0\). In the positive branch this is the familiar \(q\)-complete vanishing setting.
reconstruction: Proper exhaustion and the level-set hypothesis are restored. Existence of an arbitrary local function with a suitable Hessian is not enough.
fate: Exact fixed-degree form in \citet[Theorem~3.4.10]{hormander1965l2}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the theorem is established with these global hypotheses.

title: Andreotti--Grauert extension to complex spaces
notes: The notes attribute all these theorems for complex spaces to Andreotti and Grauert.
statement: For a strongly \(q\)-pseudoconvex complex space \(X\) and a coherent analytic sheaf \(\mathcal F\), the relevant higher cohomology groups are finite dimensional in the prescribed degree range; for \(q\)-complete spaces, \(H^j(X,\mathcal F)=0\) for \(j\ge q\). Pseudoconcave variants have ranges involving the depth of \(\mathcal F\), so they cannot be obtained merely by copying every smooth-domain formula.
reconstruction: This states the positive branch explicitly and flags the additional depth requirements for the opposite branch.
fate: Already published in \citet[\S5, finiteness and vanishing theorems]{andreottigrauert1962finitude}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the coherent-sheaf results are established; the blanket phrase requires degree and depth qualifications.

title: Runge restriction and extension of solvability
notes: For \(\omega=\{\Psi<0\}\subset\Omega\), with a Levi condition outside \(\omega\) and \(\Psi\to\infty\) at the boundary, cohomology restricts injectively. Solvability on \(\omega\) then gives solvability on \(\Omega\).
statement: A precise sufficient version is: let \(X\) have a \(C^3\) exhaustion \(\Psi\) whose regular levels outside \(X_c=\{\Psi<c\}\) satisfy \(a_q\). Then the restriction \(H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)\to H^q(X_c,\Omega_X^p)\) is injective. For relatively compact smooth sublevels the analogous statement holds for the weighted \(L^2\) cohomology with weights continuous on the closure.
reconstruction: The condition is imposed on level-set tangent hyperplanes, not replaced without justification by a signature of the full Hessian. The strict positive full-Hessian branch in the notes implies this level condition; the negative branch requires care.
fate: \citet[Theorems~3.4.6 and 3.4.9]{hormander1965l2}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the restriction theorem is established; it is an injectivity statement, not unconditional vanishing.

title: Weighted integration by parts and boundary Levi form
notes: The final displayed identity contains the weighted \(\bar\partial\) and adjoint norms, interior Hessian terms, derivative norms and the boundary Levi integral.
statement: For a smooth \((0,q)\)-form \(u\) on a smooth bounded domain, satisfying the \(\bar\partial\)-Neumann boundary condition \(\sum_j\rho_{z_j}u_{jK}=0\), the Morrey--Kohn--H\"ormander identity expresses \(\|\bar\partial u\|_\phi^2+\|\bar\partial_\phi^*u\|_\phi^2\) as the sum of coefficient \(\bar z\)-derivative norms, the weighted interior Levi form \(\sum\phi_{j\bar k}u_{jK}\overline{u_{kK}}\), and the boundary Levi form \(\sum\rho_{j\bar k}u_{jK}\overline{u_{kK}}\), with boundary measure divided by \(|\nabla\rho|\) unless \(\rho\) is normalized.
reconstruction: The boundary condition, normalization and the weighted formal adjoint are necessary for this precise identity; the general \((p,q)\) version is coefficientwise.
fate: The proof mechanism is \citet[Proposition~2.1.2, equation~(2.1.14)]{hormander1965l2}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the identity is established and explains the role of the Levi signatures.

title: Approximation of closed forms across a Runge exhaustion
notes: Closed forms in \(\omega\) are approximated by closed forms in \(\Omega\).
statement: Under the hypotheses of the preceding Runge theorem, \(\bar\partial\)-closed \((p,q-1)\)-forms on the inner sublevel are limits of restrictions of \(\bar\partial\)-closed forms on the larger domain. In the relatively compact setting the approximation is in the specified weighted \(L^2\) norm; along an exhaustion one obtains the corresponding local form of approximation.
reconstruction: The degree is \(q-1\), while the cohomological injection is in degree \(q\). No uniform-up-to-boundary approximation of arbitrary forms is inferred.
fate: Exact source: \citet[Theorems~3.4.7 and 3.4.9]{hormander1965l2}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the approximation theorem is established with the stated degree and norm.

title: Existence on a Levi-pseudoconvex bounded domain
notes: A \(C^2\) defining function with nonnegative tangential Levi form is followed by ``solvability follows'' from the identity.
statement: If \(\Omega\Subset\mathbb C^n\) has \(C^2\) pseudoconvex boundary and \(1\le q\le n\), every distributionally closed \(f\in L^2_{p,q}(\Omega)\) has a solution \(u\in L^2_{p,q-1}(\Omega)\), with \(\|u\|_2\le C_\Omega\|f\|_2\). One may use the strictly plurisubharmonic bounded weight \(|z|^2\), obtain a weighted estimate, and compare weighted and unweighted norms on the bounded domain.
reconstruction: This is solvability in \(L^2\), not smoothness of the solution up to the boundary. The notebook's comparison with grad and curl concerns the integration-by-parts mechanism.
fate: \citet[Theorem~2.2.3]{hormander1965l2}; the weighted identity is the analytic tool, not an additional regularity theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stated existence result is established.

title: Dwork rationality and the missing global hypothesis
notes: A power series convergent near zero over the complex numbers and for all \(p\)-adic metrics is said to be rational.
statement: Local convergence alone is insufficient: \(e^t=\sum t^n/n!\) has positive radius in \(\mathbb C\) and in every \(\mathbb Q_p\), but is not rational. A precise sufficient Dwork criterion is that \(F\in\mathbb Z[[t]]\) have positive complex radius and admit meromorphic continuation to the entire \(p\)-adic affine line for one prime \(p\); then \(F\in\mathbb Q(t)\).
reconstruction: Integer coefficients and global \(p\)-adic meromorphic continuation are restored. The rationality theorem is not a statement about arbitrary convergent germs at all places.
fate: \citet[Introduction and \S4]{dwork1960rationality} supplies the arithmetic-analytic argument. It was published in 1960 and available in Russian in 1961, before the seminar.
present_status: As of November 2026, the corrected criterion and rationality of finite-field zeta functions are established; the local-convergence slogan is false.

title: Zeta functions through p-adic completely continuous operators
notes: The idea is to represent the zeta function using completely continuous operators over a \(p\)-adic field.
statement: For a variety \(X/\mathbb F_q\), \(Z(X,t)=\exp(\sum_{m\ge1}\#X(\mathbb F_{q^m})t^m/m)\). Dwork's method expresses point counts through traces of suitable \(p\)-adic operators, and the resulting Fredholm determinants give \(p\)-adic meromorphic continuation. Combined with arithmetic coefficient control and the rationality criterion, this proves \(Z(X,t)\in\mathbb Q(t)\).
reconstruction: A trace or Fredholm formula alone does not automatically prove rationality of an infinite-dimensional determinant.
fate: The analytic continuation and arithmetic steps are separated in \citet[\S\S3--4]{dwork1960rationality}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the method and theorem are established; no new claim is attributed to this brief programme remark.

title: Plane distributions and the foliation existence slogan
notes: For one-dimensional foliations the question is said to reduce to vector fields; for higher codimension, existence is asserted whenever a family of planes exists.
statement: A smooth nowhere-zero line distribution is involutive and determines a one-dimensional foliation. A higher-rank plane distribution need not be involutive. The meaningful deformation question asks whether a given distribution is homotopic through plane distributions to the tangent distribution of a foliation, under specified manifold and normal-bundle hypotheses.
reconstruction: The rank-one observation is exact. The higher-rank assertion lacks the hypotheses of a general theorem and cannot be read as integrability of the given distribution.
fate: \citet[\S4.4, Theorem~4.4.2 and Corollary~4.4.3]{gromov1969stable}, received July 1968 and published in 1969, treats qualified foliation existence on open manifolds. It does not justify the unqualified notebook sentence.
present_status: As of November 2026, the broad announcement remains under-specified; Frobenius integrability and homotopy-to-foliation are distinct assertions.

title: Germs, jets and a weak homotopy equivalence
notes: The sheaf of germs and the sheaf of jets are called weakly homotopy equivalent; a global set of coefficients is said to permit construction of a function.
statement: A precise related theorem is the open invariant relation theorem: on an open smooth manifold, for the natural bundles and open diffeomorphism-invariant differential relations of Gromov's construction, the holonomic-section map to formal solutions is a weak homotopy equivalence. This is not true for an arbitrary differential relation or an arbitrary prescribed jet section.
reconstruction: Open manifold, openness, invariance and the specified natural-bundle setting are necessary qualifications. A formal solution is deformed to a holonomic one; its coefficients need not be realized without deformation.
fate: \citet[Theorem~4.1.1]{gromov1969stable}, received on 8 July 1968 and printed in 1969. Record 162 gives a fuller seminar exposition of this subject.
present_status: As of November 2026, the qualified theorem is established; the unrestricted slogan is not valid.

title: Genus zero and genus one uniformization
notes: All genus-zero compact Riemann surfaces are spheres; a genus-one surface has universal cover the complex plane and a lattice of deck translations.
statement: A connected compact Riemann surface of genus zero is biholomorphic to \(\mathbb P^1\). A connected compact genus-one surface, after choosing a point as origin, is \(E=\mathbb C/\Lambda\), where \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z\omega_1+\mathbb Z\omega_2\) is a rank-two lattice with \(\operatorname{Im}(\omega_2/\omega_1)>0\). The marked point equips it with an elliptic-curve group law.
reconstruction: The notebook initially discusses curves without a marked point; pointing is necessary for the elliptic group structure used later.
fate: Classical background to \citet[\S\S4,7]{mumford1965picard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the classification is established.

title: Lattice homothety and the modular group action
notes: Lattices differing by nonzero complex scaling give isomorphic curves; a change of integral basis yields a fractional-linear transformation.
statement: Pointed complex elliptic curves \(\mathbb C/\Lambda\) and \(\mathbb C/\Lambda'\) are isomorphic exactly when \(\Lambda'=a\Lambda\) for some \(a\in\mathbb C^*\). After normalization \(\Lambda_\tau=\mathbb Z+\mathbb Z\tau\), \(\operatorname{Im}\tau>0\), the basis-change group \(\Gamma=SL_2(\mathbb Z)\) acts by \(\tau\mapsto(a\tau+b)/(c\tau+d)\).
reconstruction: The denominator is \(c\tau+d\), as confirmed by the later formula on P000250--P000251. The P000238 denominator appears to repeat \(b\).
fate: The same presentation is used in \citet[\S7, pp.~76--78]{mumford1965picard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the lattice criterion and action are established.

title: Fundamental region and the coarse j-line
notes: The upper half-plane modulo \(SL_2(\mathbb Z)\) is depicted by the usual modular fundamental region and called the plane of elliptic curves.
statement: A standard closed fundamental region is \(\{\tau\in\mathbb H:|\operatorname{Re}\tau|\le1/2,\ |\tau|\ge1\}\), with the prescribed boundary identifications. The analytic coarse quotient \(\mathbb H/SL_2(\mathbb Z)\) is the complex affine line via the \(j\)-invariant. It classifies isomorphism classes of individual elliptic curves, but does not represent their family functor.
reconstruction: The boundary identifications and the word coarse prevent the drawing from being interpreted as a universal family.
fate: \citet[\S4 and \S7]{mumford1965picard} makes this coarse/family distinction.
present_status: As of November 2026, the coarse classification is established.

title: A family listing isomorphism classes is not yet universal
notes: A first definition asks for a family \(X\to Y\) whose fibres are the pairwise nonisomorphic objects of a class \(K\), one of each; uniqueness is then discussed.
statement: A family with one fibre in each isomorphism class is a set-theoretic parametrization. It need not be universal for families, need not exist with the proposed regularity, and has no categorical uniqueness merely from this condition. A moduli problem must also specify which families over each test base are admissible and how they pull back.
reconstruction: This preserves the progression of the lecture from a provisional definition to a functorial one.
fate: The distinction motivates \citet[Introduction and \S3]{mumford1965picard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the provisional definition is insufficient for a fine moduli problem.

title: Pullback of an analytic family
notes: The fibre product construction induces a family over a new base and has a universal property.
statement: For a holomorphic family \(\pi:X\to S\) and a holomorphic map \(f:T\to S\), the induced family is \(X\times_ST\to T\), with fibre \(X_{f(t)}\) over \(t\). In the moduli category, a morphism over \(f\) includes an isomorphism from the source family to this pullback; these isomorphisms carry the automorphism data.
reconstruction: Analytic spaces, rather than only manifolds, are allowed so that the required fibre products exist.
fate: Expository construction in \citet[\S3]{mumford1965picard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction is standard.

title: Kirillov: representability of the moduli functor
notes: Kirillov reformulates universality by assigning to a base the families over it and comparing this with maps into a moduli object.
statement: Let \(\mathcal F(S)\) be the set of isomorphism classes of admissible families over \(S\). Pullback makes \(\mathcal F\) contravariant. A fine moduli space is an object \(M\) with a natural isomorphism \(\operatorname{Hom}(-,M)\cong\mathcal F\); the universal family corresponds to \(\mathrm{id}_M\). A representing object is unique up to unique isomorphism by the Yoneda argument.
reconstruction: Isomorphism classes and naturality are essential. A family category with nontrivial automorphisms contains more information than the set-valued functor.
fate: This is the standard representability reformulation underlying \citet[\S3]{mumford1965picard}, not a new conjecture of Kirillov.
present_status: As of November 2026, the formulation and uniqueness statement are established.
speaker: A. A. Kirillov

title: Fine universality versus weaker parameter families
notes: The definitions oscillate between an inducing map existing for every family and being unique; a weaker moduli space is retained when universality fails.
statement: Fine representability requires a unique classifying map for every family and compatibility with pullback. Existence without uniqueness is a weaker parameter property; local existence near each base point is a versality property and is weaker again. A coarse moduli space has its own universal property for maps out of the moduli problem, and is not defined merely by dropping uniqueness from a universal-family assertion.
reconstruction: The three notions are separated rather than identifying all weakened formulations with coarse moduli.
fate: \citet[\S\S3--4]{mumford1965picard} supplies the relevant categories of modular families.
present_status: As of November 2026, these distinctions are standard and essential for the elliptic example.

title: Nonexistence of a fine moduli space for all pointed elliptic curves
notes: Automorphisms yield a nontrivial family with all fibres isomorphic. Its map to a one-class-per-point space would be constant, forcing a trivial family.
statement: The functor of isomorphism classes of all pointed complex elliptic families is not represented by the coarse \(j\)-line. For a fixed elliptic curve \(E\), the family over \(\mathbb C^*\) obtained by descending \(\mathbb C\times E\) under \((t,x)\mapsto(t+2\pi i,-x)\) has constant \(j\) but monodromy \(-I\) on \(H_1(E,\mathbb Z)\). It is not the product family, while pullback along a constant map from a fine one-point-per-class parameter space would be a product.
reconstruction: This explicit isotrivial twist makes the notebook's obstruction precise; the zero section descends.
fate: This is the obstruction discussed in \citet[\S\S3--4, especially pp.~58--60]{mumford1965picard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the nonrepresentability obstruction is established; the moduli stack retains the missing automorphisms.

title: Rigidification by a homology basis, not merely polarization
notes: The notes say a universal family exists for ``polarized'' curves, explained parenthetically as a chosen homology basis.
statement: For pointed complex elliptic curves with an oriented integral basis of \(H_1\), the upper half-plane is a fine analytic parameter space and the family \((\mathbb H\times\mathbb C)/\mathbb Z^2\) is universal. This is a marking or rigidification. A principal polarization alone does not eliminate the automorphism \([-1]\); for an unpointed genus-one curve, a homology marking alone also leaves translations.
reconstruction: The parenthetical basis is taken as the intended data, while the terminology ``polarized'' is corrected. Both the point and the basis are required for the stated rigidification.
fate: The analytic marked family is used in \citet[\S7]{mumford1965picard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the marked fine-moduli construction is established; the polarization-only claim would be false.

title: The moduli object represented by a topology of families
notes: A terminal object is formally adjoined when none exists; its sheaves and cohomology are then studied.
statement: The family category must retain morphisms together with fibrewise isomorphisms. Given representable isomorphism functors and an appropriate covering rule, one can study its associated site or stack and define sheaves and cohomology there. This replaces the absent universal family over an ordinary coarse parameter space, rather than asserting that formal adjunction alone creates all necessary products and descent.
reconstruction: The modern stack terminology is explanatory reconstruction; the notebook and Mumford use a topology with a formal final object.
fate: The precise construction is \citet[\S3]{mumford1965picard}, expanded in records 151--154.
present_status: As of November 2026, the method is established.

title: Automorphism groups of pointed elliptic curves
notes: Most curves have ``one automorphism'', \(x\mapsto-x\), and some have extra rotations.
statement: For a pointed complex elliptic curve, the generic origin-preserving automorphism group is cyclic of order two, consisting of the identity and \([-1]\). The square lattice has a group of order four, and the hexagonal lattice a group of order six. Thus ``one'' must mean one nonidentity automorphism in the generic case.
reconstruction: The origin-preserving condition is retained; without a marked point, all translations are automorphisms.
fate: \citet[\S4, pp.~57--59]{mumford1965picard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the automorphism calculation is established.

title: Pretopology axioms and base change revisited
notes: The fibre product is a categorical product over a base; a covering \(X_i\to X\) pulled back along \(Y\to X\) is written as a covering of \(X\).
statement: The base-changed covering is \(\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}\), not a family with target \(X\). Identity, composite-cover and pullback-cover axioms define the pretopology. A functor between the displayed site categories must preserve the specified finite limits and covers for the intended induced sheaf construction; arrow conventions for geometric morphisms must then be stated separately.
reconstruction: The displayed target is emended using the universal property and the same axiom as correctly repeated on P000245.
fate: \citet[pp.~38,41]{mumford1965picard}; compare 1967-143.1--1967-143.2.
present_status: As of November 2026, the axioms are standard, with the corrected base-change target.

title: The site of Gamma-sets
notes: Objects are \(\Gamma\)-sets, pullbacks are pairs with equal images, covers are jointly surjective, and the terminal object is a point.
statement: For a discrete group \(\Gamma\), let \(\mathcal T_\Gamma\) be the category of left \(\Gamma\)-sets and equivariant maps. A family covers if its images jointly equal the target. The fibre product has the diagonal action, and the one-point set with trivial action is terminal. This is a site even when \(\Gamma\) is infinite.
fate: Exact example in \citet[pp.~39--41]{mumford1965picard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction is established.

title: Sheaves on the group site are modules
notes: A sheaf is determined by \(A=F(\Gamma)\), with \(F(\Gamma/H)=A^H\).
statement: The category of abelian sheaves on \(\mathcal T_\Gamma\) is equivalent to the category of \(\mathbb Z[\Gamma]\)-modules. A module \(A\) gives \(F_A(S)=\operatorname{Map}_\Gamma(S,A)\); in particular \(F_A(\Gamma/H)=A^H\). The action on \(F(\Gamma)\) comes from equivariant right translations and contravariance, with a consistent left-action convention.
reconstruction: The acting subgroup in the invariant formula is \(H\); the adjacent unclear letter does not change the displayed equation.
fate: \citet[pp.~40--41]{mumford1965picard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the equivalence and orbit formula are established.

title: The value on a disjoint union is a product
notes: For a disjoint union of orbits the notes say to take a direct sum.
statement: For any disjoint union \(S=\coprod_{\alpha}S_\alpha\), the sheaf condition gives \(F_A(S)=\prod_\alpha F_A(S_\alpha)\). A direct sum agrees only for a finite family of abelian groups. In particular the constant coefficient module can yield arbitrarily supported sections on an infinite disjoint union.
reconstruction: The scan confirms the Russian words for direct sum; the mathematical correction is product.
fate: The product, explicitly printed in \citet[p.~40]{mumford1965picard}, also follows immediately from \(\operatorname{Map}_\Gamma\).
present_status: As of November 2026, the infinite-union direct-sum statement is false.

title: Cohomology of the terminal group-site object
notes: \(H^q(\cdot,F)=H^q(\Gamma,A)\).
statement: Under the sheaf-module equivalence, global sections are \(A^\Gamma\). Their right derived functors are group cohomology: \(H^q(\mathcal T_\Gamma,F_A)\cong H^q(\Gamma,A)\) for every \(q\ge0\). The terminal object's underlying set being a point does not make these groups vanish.
fate: \citet[p.~41]{mumford1965picard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the comparison is established.

title: H2 with integer coefficients and one-dimensional characters
notes: \(H^2(\Gamma,\mathbb Z)\) is identified with all one-dimensional complex representations of \(\Gamma\), without a group restriction.
statement: If \(\Gamma\) is finite, the exact sequence \(0\to\mathbb Z\to\mathbb C\xrightarrow{\exp(2\pi i\,\cdot)}\mathbb C^*\to1\), with trivial actions, gives \(H^2(\Gamma,\mathbb Z)\cong H^1(\Gamma,\mathbb C^*)=\operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma,\mathbb C^*)\), since positive-degree cohomology with coefficients in \(\mathbb C\) vanishes by averaging. More generally the same conclusion needs the relevant vanishing of \(H^1\) and \(H^2\) with \(\mathbb C\) coefficients.
reconstruction: The claim fails for \(\Gamma=\mathbb Z\): \(H^2=0\), whereas its complex characters form \(\mathbb C^*\).
fate: This is a direct application of the derived-functor formalism recalled in \citet[p.~41]{mumford1965picard}; the additional finite-group hypothesis is not visible in this September note.
present_status: As of November 2026, the corrected finite-group formula is established; the unrestricted one is false.

title: The analytic local-isomorphism topology
notes: Analytic manifolds and analytic maps are used, with jointly surjective unramified local coverings; fibre products are declared to exist.
statement: For a fixed complex analytic space \(X\), the analytic \(\acute{e}\)tale site has local biholomorphisms \(U\to X\) as objects and jointly surjective families as covers. Its fibre products exist. If one instead uses all holomorphic maps among all analytic manifolds, arbitrary fibre products need not remain manifolds; the larger category of analytic spaces repairs this, as the next lecture explicitly acknowledges.
reconstruction: Discreteness of fibres alone does not mean unramified: \(z\mapsto z^2\) has discrete fibres but ramifies at zero.
fate: \citet[\S2, pp.~44--45]{mumford1965picard}; the internal correction is occurrence 1968-152.1.
present_status: As of November 2026, the analytic-space site is established; the blanket manifold pullback assertion is false.

title: Comparison with ordinary analytic sheaf cohomology
notes: The topology's cohomology on \(X\) equals the cohomology of the restricted sheaf on the usual topology because coverings split locally.
statement: The inclusion of ordinary open subsets of a complex analytic space \(X\) into its local-biholomorphism site induces an equivalence of sheaf categories. For an abelian sheaf \(F\), \(H^q(X_{\mathrm{an},\acute{e}t},F)\cong H^q(X,F|_{\mathrm{opens}})\). Locally each local biholomorphism is an isomorphism onto an ordinary open subset, providing the comparison basis.
reconstruction: This is an analytic local-isomorphism comparison; it is not an assertion that algebraic \(\acute{e}\)tale cohomology with arbitrary coefficients equals ordinary topology over every field.
fate: \citet[pp.~44--45]{mumford1965picard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the comparison is established.

title: The site of families and cohomology of an individual family
notes: Objects are analytic families \(\pi:X\to S\), morphisms induce pullbacks, and covers are covers of bases. The cohomology of \(\pi\) is that of \(S\).
statement: For a fixed family \(\pi\), the local-isomorphism site of its pullbacks \(X\times_SU\to U\) is equivalent to the local-isomorphism site of \(S\). Thus a sheaf restricted to this slice has the corresponding cohomology \(H^q(S,F_\pi)\). Morphisms of families include a Cartesian square and its chosen fibrewise isomorphism.
reconstruction: The identification is for the slice over the particular family. It does not identify the cohomology of the entire moduli problem with the cohomology of one arbitrary base.
fate: The family-site construction is \citet[\S3]{mumford1965picard}; compare its induced-topology definition on p.~42.
present_status: As of November 2026, the slice comparison is established.

title: Products over the formal moduli object are isomorphism spaces
notes: The direct product of two families cannot simply have base \(S_1\times S_2\); the notes later count automorphisms as multiplicities. An earlier sentence says a curve's product with itself is itself.
statement: For proper smooth pointed genus-one families, or smooth proper curves of genus at least two, the product over the moduli object has base \(I=\operatorname{Isom}_{S_1\times S_2}(\operatorname{pr}_1^*X_1,\operatorname{pr}_2^*X_2)\). A point consists of \((s_1,s_2,\alpha)\) with \(\alpha:X_{1,s_1}\cong X_{2,s_2}\). Its fibre over \((s_1,s_2)\) is empty if the curves are nonisomorphic and otherwise a torsor under their automorphism group. A self-product therefore has one point for each automorphism, not necessarily one point.
reconstruction: The Isom space is an analytic space; smoothness or local biholomorphy requires additional conditions on the families. The lower-page multiplicity remark corrects the preceding set-level simplification.
fate: Exact construction in \citet[\S3, pp.~49--53]{mumford1965picard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the Isom construction is established and retains the automorphism information lost by a coarse quotient.

title: Coverings of the formal terminal object
notes: A family \(\{\pi_i\to M\}\) covers if for every \(\pi\), the products \(\pi_i\times_M\pi\to\pi\) form a genuine covering. All families together need not be a covering.
statement: An atlas family covers the moduli object when every base change by an admissible family is represented by a jointly surjective family of local isomorphisms of bases. This requires both local deformation completeness and the appropriate unramified condition. Merely listing a representative of every curve, or including every possible family, does not ensure that each component map is eligible as an \(\acute{e}\)tale cover.
reconstruction: The covering class is fixed before applying joint surjectivity; adding non-\(\acute{e}\)tale families is not automatically permitted.
fate: \citet[\S3, pp.~50--54]{mumford1965picard}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the base-change test is established.

title: Analytic spaces are required for general fibre products
notes: The opening apology says that everywhere one should read analytic spaces, not analytic manifolds, because fibre products must exist.
statement: The category of complex analytic spaces admits fibre products of holomorphic maps. The subcategory of manifolds does not: the pullback of \(z\mapsto z^2\) along the map of a point to zero is the nonreduced analytic space with local ring \(\mathbb C\{z\}/(z^2)\). Even among reduced spaces, the equation \(x^2=y^2\) gives a singular pullback.
reconstruction: Nonreduced structure is retained in the first example; passing only to point sets would erase the obstruction. This is the lecturer's own correction, not a modern conjectural emendation.
fate: The distinction is already built into \citet[\S\S2--3]{mumford1965picard}. It corrects occurrence 1968-151.7.
present_status: As of November 2026, the category correction is established and necessary.

title: Fibre products and the three covering axioms repeated
notes: The universal square and its unique factorization are redrawn, followed by composition, identity and pullback of covers.
statement: For maps \(X\to Z\leftarrow Y\), \(X\times_ZY\) represents compatible pairs of maps into \(X,Y\). A pretopology has identity covers, composites of covering families as covers, and base-changed covers \(X_i\times_XY\to Y\). These statements include the existence of the indicated pullbacks.
reconstruction: The undeciphered letter above the self-map \(X\to X\) is understood as the identity map, as required by the axiom; no further mathematical content is assigned to the cancelled word.
fate: Already given in \citet[p.~38]{mumford1965picard}; this is a recurrence of 1967-143.1--1967-143.2 and 1968-151.1.
present_status: As of November 2026, the formulation is standard.

title: Abelian presheaves and effective gluing
notes: A presheaf is contravariant, and a sheaf has a unique global section inducing every compatible family of local sections.
statement: An abelian presheaf is a functor \(F:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Ab}\). For each cover \(\{U_i\to U\}\), the map \(F(U)\to\prod_iF(U_i)\) identifies \(F(U)\) with the equalizer of the two restrictions to \(\prod_{i,j}F(U_i\times_UU_j)\). Thus compatibility is equality after the two projections, and both existence and uniqueness are required.
fate: \citet[p.~39]{mumford1965picard}; a repeated definition rather than an additional theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026, the definition is established.

title: Canonical sheafification
notes: A parenthesis asserts a canonical procedure turning every presheaf into a sheaf for any topology.
statement: For a site, the inclusion of abelian sheaves into abelian presheaves has a left adjoint \(F\mapsto aF\), characterized by \(\operatorname{Hom}(aF,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,G)\) for sheaves \(G\). For abelian groups sheafification is exact. In particular a presheaf may be nonzero while its associated sheaf vanishes because its sections vanish locally.
reconstruction: The universal property and exactness specify the construction used in the following comparison criterion; no claim that sections are unchanged is made.
