fate: This is standard machinery in \citet[\S1]{mumford1965picard} and the sheaf-theoretic framework of \citet[\S3]{grothendieck1957homological}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction is established.

title: Derived cohomology, exact sequences and injective acyclicity
notes: The notes prescribe \(H^0(U,F)=F(U)\), a long exact sequence for short exact sequences, enough injectives, and zero cohomology for injective sheaves.
statement: The category of abelian sheaves on a site has enough injectives. Deriving the left-exact sections functor gives \(H^q(U,F)\), with \(H^0(U,F)=F(U)\), functorial connecting morphisms, and the long exact cohomology sequence. An injective sheaf \(I\) has \(H^q(U,I)=0\) for \(q>0\); its degree-zero sections need not vanish.
reconstruction: The omitted positive-degree qualification is restored. Cohomology on \(U\) means cohomology in the slice site.
fate: \citet[pp.~37--39]{mumford1965picard}; \citet[\S\S2--3]{grothendieck1957homological}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the corrected derived-functor assertions are established.

title: Local-acyclicity criterion for comparison of sites
notes: For a structure-compatible functor \(f:T_1\to T_2\), the notation \(f^*F(U)=F(f(U))\) is used. If the sheaf associated with \(U\mapsto H^i(f(U),F)\) is zero, the displayed cohomology map is an isomorphism.
statement: Let a functor \(u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D\) induce a geometric morphism \(f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\) whose direct image is \(f_*F(U)=F(uU)\), and suppose the global-sections functors compose in the usual way. If \(R^if_*F=0\) for every \(i>0\), the Leray spectral sequence gives \(H^q(\mathcal C,f_*F)\cong H^q(\mathcal D,F)\). The higher direct image is computed by sheafifying the presheaf of cohomology over the inverse-image slices; when these are represented by \(uU\), this is \(U\mapsto H^i(\mathcal D/uU,F)\). The same criterion applies to the corresponding slices over an object.
reconstruction: The notebook's star labels precomposition, which is the direct-image functor for the geometric morphism in this convention. The positive-degree condition and the precise slice interpretation are supplied; a condition at \(i=0\) would generally force the coefficient sheaf itself to vanish.
fate: The exact application appears in \citet[\S7, p.~80, vanishing of \(R^iy_*\) for \(i>0\)]{mumford1965picard}; the homological argument is the Leray formalism of \citet[\S3]{grothendieck1957homological}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the criterion is established under the indicated functorial and acyclicity hypotheses.

title: A terminal moduli object and its candidate atlas
notes: A new category \(T_M\) adjoins a terminal object. Candidate covering families must contain every isomorphism type, with each type occurring only discretely.
statement: For a moduli category with representable isomorphism functors, an atlas is a family of objects whose maps to the moduli object are locally isomorphisms in the chosen topology and are jointly surjective after every base change. Meeting every isomorphism class is the pointwise-surjectivity part; discrete occurrence is a necessary unramified-type condition in this setting. Those two conditions alone do not prove local universality or the existence of the required pullbacks.
reconstruction: The local extension requirement on the next page supplies information beyond the two enumerated conditions. Formal adjunction of a terminal object is not treated as an existence proof for a fine moduli space.
fate: The precise modular-family construction is \citet[\S3, pp.~49--54]{mumford1965picard}; compare 1968-151.10--1968-151.11.
present_status: As of November 2026, the atlas construction is established for the stated moduli problem, with the local hypotheses retained.

title: Local extension property of a modular family
notes: A morphism from a subfamily over a submanifold is required to extend locally to a neighbourhood in the base of an arbitrary family; the picture calls it a tubular neighbourhood.
statement: A sufficient precise version is the following. Let \(X\to S\) be a modular analytic family such that, for every test family \(Y\to T\), its isomorphism space \(I=\operatorname{Isom}(Y,X)\to T\) is a local biholomorphism. A family morphism defined on an analytic subspace \(T_0\subset T\) gives a section of \(I\to T\) over \(T_0\). Near each point of \(T_0\), the inverse of the appropriate local biholomorphic branch extends that section, hence extends the family morphism.
reconstruction: This is a local assertion, not a global extension theorem or existence of a holomorphic tubular neighbourhood for every analytic subspace. The displayed crossed arrow does not uniquely encode a stronger formal deformation criterion.
fate: The isomorphism-space criterion and modular families are treated in \citet[\S3, pp.~50--54]{mumford1965picard}. The notebook gives an informal extension formulation of this mechanism.
present_status: As of November 2026, the precise local lifting statement is established; the broad tubular-neighbourhood wording needs the reconstruction above.

title: Resolving compatibility conditions for a differential system
notes: The Spencer resolution is presented as a method for solving \(p(x,D)u=w\), with a matrix \(p\) and vector-valued unknown and data.
statement: A differential operator \(P:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F\) of order \(\mu\) factors as \(\mathcal E\xrightarrow{j_\mu}J_\mu E\xrightarrow{p_\mu}F\). Prolonged equations and their compatibility operators yield Spencer complexes under constant-rank and regularity hypotheses. Their formal exactness is distinct from exactness on smooth sections. A locally exact compatibility complex gives local solvability for data satisfying its next compatibility equation; the unrestricted-jet resolution alone does not prove this for every \(P\).
reconstruction: The hypotheses are restored at the level of the method. Neither formal integrability nor the use of jets is presented as an unconditional smooth existence theorem.
fate: The expressly named source is \citet[Introduction; Chapter~I, \S3 and Proposition~8.3]{sweeney1968neumann}, received 4 September 1966, revised 30 November 1967, and printed June 1968. It gives exactness results for regular constant-coefficient systems and real-analytic germs under its stated hypotheses. Compare \citet[\S\S1.2,1.6]{spencer1969overdetermined}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the method and its specified applications are established; no general smooth-solvability claim follows from the note.

title: Finite jet bundles and an injective map of sheaves
notes: For the sheaf \(\mathcal O\) of smooth-function germs, \(j_\mu:\mathcal O\to J_\mu\) is said to be an embedding. The zeroth-order case is followed by an ambiguous zero symbol.
statement: On a smooth \(n\)-manifold, \(J_\mu\) is the vector bundle of \(\mu\)-jets of scalar functions. A local section of this bundle has coordinates \(\phi_I(x)\), \(0\le |I|\le\mu\), using unnormalized derivatives. Prolongation sends \(f\) to the section \(j_\mu f=(\partial^If)_I\). As a map of sheaves of real vector spaces it is injective because its zeroth component is \(f\). It is not the evaluation map from a function germ to its finite jet at one point, which is not injective. For \(\mu=0\), \(J_0\cong\mathcal O\) and \(j_0\) is the identity.
reconstruction: Bundles, sheaves of their sections, and individual jet fibres are distinguished. The subsequent map at order zero is to zero, yielding \(0\to\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}\mathcal O\to0\).
fate: \citet[Chapter~I, \S1 and Proposition~6.2]{sweeney1968neumann}; \citet[\S\S1.1,1.3]{spencer1969overdetermined}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction and sheaf-level injectivity are established.

title: Holonomic jet sections are characterized by derivative compatibility
notes: The notes first compare \(\partial\phi_0/\partial x_j\) with \(\phi_j\), then require \(\partial_j\phi_I=\phi_{I+1_j}\) for every \(|I|\le\mu-1\).
statement: A smooth local jet section \(\phi=(\phi_I)_{|I|\le\mu}\) is holonomic, meaning \(\phi=j_\mu f\) for a smooth function \(f\), if and only if \(\partial_j\phi_I=\phi_{I+e_j}\) for all \(j\) and \(|I|\le\mu-1\). Necessity follows by differentiation; sufficiency follows inductively from \(f=\phi_0\). For normalized Taylor coefficients the formula would instead contain the corresponding multi-index factors.
reconstruction: The derivative rather than Taylor-coefficient normalization is fixed by the first-order example. Gelfand's intervention is the coordinate presentation, not a separate conjecture.
fate: This is the kernel statement in \citet[Chapter~I, Proposition~5.1(ii)]{sweeney1968neumann} and \citet[equation~(1.3.2)]{spencer1969overdetermined}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the criterion is established and directly verified by induction.

title: The Spencer operator as actual minus formal differentiation
notes: The first operator is \(\sum_j(\partial_j\phi_I-\phi_{I+e_j})dx_j\), and its continuation is called \(D=d-\delta\).
statement: For a jet-valued differential form \(\phi\in\Omega^r\otimes J_k\), the Spencer operator is locally \((D\phi)_I=\sum_j dx_j\wedge(\partial_j\phi_I-\phi_{I+e_j})\), \(|I|\le k-1\). Thus \(D:\Omega^r\otimes J_k\to\Omega^{r+1}\otimes J_{k-1}\). It is a globally defined first-order differential operator; in these coordinates it is the difference of actual and formal exterior differentiation. The two summands separately depend on coordinates, whereas their difference does not.
reconstruction: The formula includes exterior degree, jet order, and the order of wedge factors. It is not linear over smooth functions for the usual module structures.
fate: \citet[Chapter~I, \S5, equation~(5.4)]{sweeney1968neumann}; \citet[equation~(1.3.1)\(^{\prime}\)]{spencer1969overdetermined}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the operator is established; its invariant character is essential to the resolution.

title: The one-form formula requires a wedge-order correction
notes: The displayed continuation is \(d(\phi_I^jdx_j)-\phi_{I+e_s}^jdx_j\wedge dx_s\), with the derivative-index correction also unclear.
statement:
With \(D=d-\delta\) as in the preceding degree-zero formula, the correct expression is 
\[
D(\phi_I^jdx_j)=\sum_{s,j}(\partial_s\phi_I^j-\phi_{I+e_s}^j)\,dx_s\wedge dx_j.
\]
Equivalently the formal term is \(+\sum_{s,j}\phi_{I+e_s}^jdx_j\wedge dx_s\). Retaining the printed minus sign together with the reversed wedge order is inconsistent with the previous definition and does not generally give \(D^2=0\).
reconstruction: The scan confirms the displayed order \(dx_j\wedge dx_s\); the choice \(e_s\) is dictated by the differentiation direction. The repair is mathematical, not a claim that the transcription omitted a legible sign.
fate: The corrected order is explicit in \citet[equation~(1.3.1)\(^{\prime}\)]{spencer1969overdetermined}; compare \citet[Chapter~I, equation~(5.4)]{sweeney1968neumann}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the literal sign-and-order combination is false; the corrected formula gives the standard differential.

title: The finite exact Spencer sequence for unrestricted jets
notes: The sequence \(\mathcal O\to J_\mu\to T^*\otimes J_{\mu-1}\to\Lambda^2T^*\otimes J_{\mu-2}\to\cdots\) is said to terminate and be exact.
statement:
For every \(\mu\ge0\), the sequence of sheaves of real vector spaces 
\[
0\longrightarrow\mathcal C^\infty_M\xrightarrow{j_\mu}J_\mu\xrightarrow D\Omega^1\otimes J_{\mu-1}\xrightarrow D\cdots\xrightarrow D\Omega^n\otimes J_{\mu-n}\longrightarrow0
\]
is exact, with \(J_k=0\) for \(k<0\). The identities \(d^2=\delta^2=0\) and \(d\delta+\delta d=0\) give \(D^2=0\); exactness follows inductively in jet order using the exact polynomial Koszul complex for the highest-order symbols. The same result holds for the jet bundle of any smooth vector bundle.
reconstruction: This resolves the sheaf of unrestricted smooth sections. For a subbundle of jets defined by a differential equation, exactness is a separate analytic issue, as explained in 1968-153.1. The individual maps are not morphisms of the usual smooth-function module structures.
fate: Exact publication match: \citet[Chapter~I, Proposition~6.2, p.~238]{sweeney1968neumann}; reproduced as equation~(1.3.3) with proof in \citet[\S1.3]{spencer1969overdetermined}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the finite jet resolution is established and was available before the seminar.

title: The unresolved comparison with a higher-order pseudo-object
notes: A marginal comparison reads either \ru{псевдогр.} or \ru{псевдооп.}, followed by ``one order higher''.
statement: No mathematical assertion beyond the legible jet construction can be uniquely recovered from this phrase. The first reading might refer to pseudogroups and the second to an operator construction, but the note does not supply a definition or a formula deciding between them.
reconstruction: Neither reading is silently promoted to an additional theorem; the names listed above it belong to the surrounding Spencer-theory attribution.
fate: \citet[Introduction and bibliography]{sweeney1968neumann} explicitly connects Spencer theory with pseudogroups, making that reading plausible but not conclusive. The alternative remains a transcription ambiguity.
present_status: As of November 2026, the marginal comparison remains unidentified; it is not an open mathematical problem.

title: Pointed elliptic families and Cartesian morphisms
notes: The objects are analytic families of complex tori with a distinguished section \(\sigma:S\to X\).
statement: An analytic family of pointed elliptic curves is a proper smooth holomorphic map \(\pi:E\to S\) with connected genus-one fibres, together with a holomorphic section \(e:S\to E\). Morphisms consist of a map of bases and a section-preserving isomorphism with the pulled-back family. The section makes each fibre an elliptic group curve and removes translation automorphisms, but retains the origin-preserving finite automorphisms.
reconstruction: Properness, smoothness and connected fibres specify the intended family category; arbitrary maps with pointwise torus fibres are not silently admitted.
fate: The category is the elliptic-curve case of \citet[\S4]{mumford1965picard}; see also \citet[\S2]{hain2008moduli}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the definition is established.

title: The coarse j-line has no smooth family realizing its identity parameter
notes: The quotient \(S'=\mathbb H/\Gamma\) is called coarse; the notes say there is a family with base \(S'\), then explain that the family over \(\mathbb H\) is not induced from it and that isotrivial twists are missed.
statement: For \(\Gamma=SL_2(\mathbb Z)\), the coarse quotient is the \(j\)-line. There is no smooth pointed elliptic family over the whole coarse line whose \(j\)-invariant is the identity. Locally near the square or hexagonal elliptic point, a family over a disc has a lifted period map to \(\mathbb H\); the coarse map is locally a square or cube of a local coordinate, so it cannot compose to a simple parameter on that disc. Separately, nontrivial isotrivial twists show that a pointwise classifying coarse map cannot classify all families.
reconstruction: The statement ``there is a family'' is false if it means one realizing each coarse parameter, as the surrounding discussion suggests. Trivial families over the line certainly exist but do not have the required classifying map. The two obstructions are distinguished.
fate: The exceptional local parameters are discussed in \citet[\S4, p.~59]{mumford1965picard}. The local lifting obstruction and isotrivial construction are explicit in \citet[Exercises~25--26, \S3.6]{hain2008moduli}. This repeats GP-1968-01.
present_status: As of November 2026, the coarse-versus-fine distinction and nonexistence are established.

title: The marked universal family and its modular action
notes: The family is \((\mathbb H\times\mathbb C)/((\tau,z)\sim(\tau,z+m\tau+n))\). The group acts by \(\tau'=(a\tau+b)/(c\tau+d)\), \(z'=z/(c\tau+d)\).
statement: The quotient \(\mathcal E_{\mathbb H}=(\mathbb H\times\mathbb C)/\mathbb Z^2\), with translations \(z\mapsto z+m\tau+n\), is a holomorphic family with zero section and a distinguished oriented homology basis. Every \(\gamma=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{smallmatrix}\right)\in SL_2(\mathbb Z)\) lifts by the displayed formula because \((c\tau+d)^{-1}(\mathbb Z\tau+\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z\gamma\tau+\mathbb Z\). The quotient family over the analytic stack \([\mathbb H/SL_2(\mathbb Z)]\) is universal in the family-category sense.
reconstruction: The notebook's underlined ``problem'' is the task of specifying this lifted action, answered on the next page; it is not a newly open problem. Stack notation is modern reconstruction.
fate: \citet[\S7]{mumford1965picard}; an explicit modern formulation is \citet[\S3.6, Theorem~3.18]{hain2008moduli}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction and action are established.

title: Three marked boundary points represent two exceptional orbits
notes: The fundamental-domain drawing marks three fixed points and says that branching occurs there.
statement: For the effective \(PSL_2(\mathbb Z)\)-action on \(\mathbb H\), there are two orbits with nontrivial stabilizers, represented by \(i\) and \(e^{2\pi i/3}\), with orders two and three. The two boundary representatives of the hexagonal orbit account for the third marked point in a closed fundamental domain. For \(SL_2(\mathbb Z)\), \(-I\) fixes every base point, so the generic stabilizer is \(C_2\), and the exceptional stabilizers are \(C_4,C_6\).
reconstruction: Counting points drawn in one closed domain is separated from counting orbits and from the non-effective central action.
fate: \citet[\S4]{mumford1965picard}; \citet[\S3.5, Example~3.14]{hain2008moduli}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the stabilizer and branching descriptions are established after this qualification.

title: Constant coefficients and the cohomology of one family
notes: The coefficient sheaf has one copy of \(\mathbb Z\) for each connected component, and \(H^q(\pi,\mathbb Z)=H^q(S,\mathbb Z)\).
statement: On the local-isomorphism slice over a family \(\pi:E\to S\), the constant coefficient sheaf assigns locally constant integer-valued functions to each base. If a base \(U\) is locally connected, this group is \(\prod_{\pi_0(U)}\mathbb Z\). The slice-site comparison identifies \(H^q(\pi,\mathbb Z)\) with ordinary sheaf cohomology \(H^q(S,\mathbb Z)\). These are not the cohomology groups of the total space \(E\), nor yet those of the terminal moduli object.
reconstruction: The finite three-summand drawing is harmless; for an infinite set of components one must take a product. Connected components are open for the analytic spaces under discussion.
fate: The comparison uses \citet[\S\S2--3]{mumford1965picard} and repeats 1968-151.8--1968-151.9 with specified coefficients.
present_status: As of November 2026, the slice identification is established.

title: The level-three subsite and comparison with group cohomology
notes: A subcategory of \(\Gamma\)-sets has point stabilizers inside \(\Gamma_3\). The assignment \(S\mapsto(\mathbb H\times S)/\Gamma\) induces a cohomology isomorphism after adjoining terminal objects.
statement: Let \(\Gamma=SL_2(\mathbb Z)\) and \(\Gamma(3)=\ker(\Gamma\to SL_2(\mathbb Z/3))\). This subgroup is torsion-free. For a discrete \(\Gamma\)-set \(S\) with all stabilizers contained in \(\Gamma(3)\), the diagonal action on \(\mathbb H\times S\) is free and its quotient is a complex analytic base carrying the descended elliptic family. These objects form the comparison subsite. Contractibility of \(\mathbb H\), local acyclicity and the covering criterion give \(H^q(\mathcal M_{1,1}^{\mathrm{an}},\mathbb Z)\cong H^q(\Gamma,\mathbb Z)\).
reconstruction: The freeness is for the diagonal action on these admissible objects; the full modular action on the upper half-plane is not free. The formal terminal object is adjoined because the one-point \(\Gamma\)-set does not satisfy the stabilizer restriction.
fate: Exact construction and comparison: \citet[\S7, pp.~79--80]{mumford1965picard}. The classifying-space interpretation is \citet[Proposition~3.13]{hain2008moduli}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the comparison is established.

title: Integral cohomology of the elliptic moduli site is periodic
notes: The formula is transcribed as \(H^q(M,\mathbb Z)=0\) for \(q\ne2\), and \(\mathbb Z_{12}\) for \(q=2\); the degree sign is heavily retraced.
statement:
For the uncompactified analytic moduli stack of pointed elliptic curves,
\[
H^q(\mathcal M_{1,1}^{\mathrm{an}},\mathbb Z)=
\begin{cases}\mathbb Z,&q=0,\\\mathbb Z/12,&q>0\text{ even},\\0,&q\text{ odd}.\end{cases}
\]
More precisely its ring is \(\mathbb Z[c]/(12c)\), with \(|c|=2\). This differs both from the coarse \(j\)-line, whose positive-degree integral cohomology vanishes, and from the compactified moduli stack.
reconstruction: The higher-degree correction follows from \(SL_2(\mathbb Z)\cong C_4*_{C_2}C_6\). In every positive even degree the Mayer--Vietoris map \(\mathbb Z/4\oplus\mathbb Z/6\to\mathbb Z/2\) is \((a,b)\mapsto a-b\) modulo two, is surjective, and has cyclic kernel of order twelve. The odd groups vanish; degree zero is \(\mathbb Z\). Choosing the degree-two class restricting to generators of both cyclic groups gives the displayed ring. This is an explicit verification of a correction, not a novel cohomology theorem.
fate: The moduli-to-group comparison is \citet[\S7]{mumford1965picard}; the degree-one and degree-two computation and group presentation are in \citet[Proposition~3.13 and presentation~(3)]{hain2008moduli}. The periodic extension is verified by the amalgam calculation above.
present_status: As of November 2026, the corrected integral cohomology is established; the literal concentration in degree two is false.

title: The assertion over other fields concerns the Picard group
notes: The notes say that the answer remains true over any field of characteristic different from two.
statement: For every field \(k\), the algebraic Picard group of the stack of elliptic curves is \(\operatorname{Pic}(\mathcal M_{1,1,k})\cong\mathbb Z/12\), generated by the Hodge line bundle. This is a statement about invertible sheaves. Ordinary integral Betti cohomology is the complex-analytic invariant of the preceding item and is not defined by that formula for an arbitrary field.
reconstruction: The text switches invariants without explaining the comparison. Mumford's theorem as published assumes characteristic different from both two and three. Its Picard conclusion over fields of characteristic three, and indeed two, has a later exact extension; this does not extend the entire displayed Betti-cohomology table to all fields.
fate: \citet[\S6, Main Theorem, p.~73]{mumford1965picard} proves the characteristic-not-two-or-three case. \citet[Theorem~1.1]{fultonolsson2010picard}, circulated on 17 April 2007 and published in 2010, proves \(\operatorname{Pic}(\mathcal M_{1,1,S})\cong\mathbb Z/12\oplus\operatorname{Pic}(\mathbb A^1_S)\) for reduced \(S\), or when two is invertible on \(S\). For \(S=\operatorname{Spec}k\), the second summand is zero.
present_status: As of November 2026, the algebraic Picard assertion is established for every field. The literal general-field cohomology statement is under-specified until its invariant and topology are fixed.

title: What the invariant modulo twelve means for a family
notes: A boxed conclusion says that families have an invariant modulo twelve.
statement: The universal Hodge line bundle \(\lambda\) generates the cyclic Picard group of order twelve. For a smooth pointed elliptic family \(\pi:E\to S\), its pullback is \(\lambda_S=\pi_*\Omega^1_{E/S}\), and the nonvanishing discriminant gives a canonical trivialization of \(\lambda_S^{\otimes12}\). In the complex analytic setting, \(c_1(\lambda_S)\in H^2(S,\mathbb Z)\) is the pullback of the universal order-twelve class and is killed by twelve.
reconstruction: A family over an arbitrary base does not automatically yield a scalar in \(\mathbb Z/12\). It yields a line-bundle class, or its cohomology class on that base, whose universal source has order twelve.
fate: \citet[\S6]{mumford1965picard}; \citet[Introduction, equations~(1-3)--(1-7)]{fultonolsson2010picard}; the analytic generator is \citet[Theorem~6.6]{hain2008moduli}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the Hodge-line interpretation and its order-twelve relation are established.

title: Shafarevich: a site of transverse patches and holonomy
notes: For an ordinary differential equation, objects are transverse patches and maps follow trajectories to another patch. A fibre product is drawn.
statement: For a nonsingular smooth foliation, choose a complete transversal \(T\). Germs of holonomy maps between open subsets of \(T\) form an \(\acute{e}\)tale groupoid \(G\). Equivariant sheaves on \(T\), or the corresponding local site with ordinary open covers and holonomy identifications, retain the transverse topology and isotropy of the foliation. Fibre products of local transverse maps exist locally after restricting patches. Singular points require an additional definition and are not covered by this nonsingular construction.
reconstruction: The holonomy-groupoid interpretation makes the drawing precise but is a modern reconstruction. The note does not say whether path data, holonomy germs or only pointwise trajectory incidence define its morphisms; those choices can produce different groupoids.
fate: A precise later development is \citet[\S\S1.1,2.1--2.2 and Theorem~3.1]{moerdijk1991foliations}: the classifying topos of an \(\acute{e}\)tale groupoid agrees in homotopy and cohomology with its classifying space. This matches the transverse-site method, not the unqualified singular-flow or Euler formula in the next remarks. The paper appeared in 1991; no earlier circulation date was verified.
present_status: As of November 2026, the nonsingular holonomy-site construction is established; the exact morphism convention of this notebook example remains only partially identified.
speaker: I. R. Shafarevich

title: For a genuine leaf fibration the transverse cohomology is that of the base
notes: The abbreviated sentence says that, for a fibration, the cohomology of the base and the system are \ru{трив.}, and mentions a final object.
statement: If a foliation is the foliation by connected fibres of a surjective smooth submersion \(p:M\to B\) with manifold leaf space \(B\), its holonomy groupoid on a complete transversal is equivalent to the \(\acute{e}\)tale groupoid presenting \(B\). Its classifying topos is therefore equivalent to ordinary sheaves on \(B\), and the corresponding cohomology groups agree. They need not vanish: a nonempty connected base has \(H^0(B,\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z\).
reconstruction: The abbreviation may mean that the identification is trivial, rather than that both cohomologies vanish. The Russian and scan do not decide the omitted predicate. The existence of a terminal object by itself never forces positive-degree cohomology to vanish.
fate: The groupoid invariance is \citet[\S2.2]{moerdijk1991foliations}; for a groupoid presenting a space the classifying topos is its usual sheaf topos, as explained in \S2.4 of that paper. The fibration case follows directly.
present_status: As of November 2026, the base comparison is established; a reading asserting vanishing is false and the notebook wording remains ambiguous.
speaker: I. R. Shafarevich

title: Euler characteristic as a difference of cycle and singular-point counts
notes: For an equation on the plane and the constant sheaf of its Grothendieck topology, the Euler characteristic is said to be the difference between the number of limit cycles and the number of singular points.
statement: No precise theorem is determined without specifying the vector-field class, treatment of singular leaves, cohomology theory and support condition, finiteness of the relevant groups, and which signed difference is intended. For example, for the constant nonzero horizontal vector field on \(\mathbb R^2\), the ordinary transverse leaf space is \(\mathbb R\), with ordinary constant-sheaf Euler characteristic one, while both stated counts are zero. Thus the unrestricted ordinary-cohomology interpretation is false.
reconstruction: The counterexample does not identify the author's intended compact-support, reduced or relative invariant. It demonstrates why the omitted convention is substantive. The phrase does not supply a definite open problem, and no problem-index entry is invented.
fate: Searches combining the named speaker, transverse sites, Euler characteristic, singular points and limit cycles did not identify a publication with these exact hypotheses and conclusion. \citet[Theorem~3.1]{moerdijk1991foliations} provides the general cohomological framework but no such cycle-count formula.
present_status: As of November 2026, the intended invariant and theorem remain unidentified; the broad ordinary-cohomology reading is refuted by the stated elementary example.
